strengths: Exceptional empirical rigor with evaluation across 6 model families and 7+ datasets using multiple validation paradigms (ablation, steering, geometric analysis, layer-wise verification)
Novel TSLA method that principally addresses limitations of prior DLA approach through task subspace projection and handles label hyperparameter sensitivity
Clear mechanistic insights with strong empirical support: TR heads align with task subspace, TL heads rotate within it, with theoretical grounding (Theorem 1)
Well-articulated contribution reconciling introspective and holistic research paradigms on ICL, with clear explanation of TR-IH relationship
Task-type dependent findings (TR vectors for classification, TL for generation) demonstrate sophisticated understanding of mechanisms
Excellent presentation with clear figures, comprehensive appendices enabling reproducibility, and promised code release
Demonstrates TR/TL separability through independent ablation effects with novel TR Ratio metric
Consistent findings across diverse models establish generality within classification domain
weaknesses: Limited task scope: evaluation restricted primarily to 7 simple text classification datasets (2-6 labels); only one synthetic generation task; no complex reasoning, mathematical, or multi-hop tasks, restricting generalizability claims

Strong unrealistic assumptions in Theorem 1 (Grassmannian distribution of label unembeddings) that don't hold in practice where learned representations have structure; bounds weaken with more subspaces
TR/TL framework limitations: definition as 'label space recognition' is awkward for open-ended generation, requiring workarounds (hardcoding tokens in Section I.2) that suggest limited generality

Key experimental choices lack sensitivity analysis: 3% threshold for head selection, 8-shot demonstrations, midpoint layer for steering injection, 75% depth for geometry measurement—results may be sensitive to these
Causality claims stronger than evidence: ablation shows importance but not mechanism; steering uses artificial injection; no analysis of compensation by other heads or why heads learn these roles
Incomplete comparison with concurrent work (Yang et al. 2025, Jiang et al. 2025) studying similar geometric aspects; limited discussion of relationship to function vector heads literature
Limited failure case analysis: no investigation of when TR/TL decomposition breaks down, performance with adversarial demonstrations, or edge cases; unclear generality boundaries
TSLA method requires clear label token identification and assumes meaningful label unembedding subspace; applicability to multi-label, truly open-ended, or structured tasks undefined

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 6 models and 7+ datasets with multiple validation approaches (overlap, ablation, steering, geometry)
Novel TSLA method that improves upon Direct Logit Attribution with principled handling of label robustness and label discrimination
Multiple independent lines of evidence convincingly demonstrating TR/TL separation, including new TR ratio metric
Interesting empirical findings reconciling prior work on Induction Heads and providing layer-wise organizational insights
Strong experimental hygiene with detailed reproducibility information and extensive supplementary materials
Clear geometric intuition for TR head alignment and TL head rotation mechanisms
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: TR/TL decomposition from Pan et al. (2023); TSLA application to attention heads is incremental
Theorem 1 makes unrealistic assumptions (uniformly random semantic subspaces from Grassmannian) with unclear connection to practical TSLA effectiveness
Narrow evaluation scope: dominated by simple classification (7/8 tasks), limited to 8-shot ICL setting only, single simple generation task, only decoder-only models
Critical design choices lack justification: why 3% threshold (no sensitivity analysis), why normalize TL by TR score, validity of label-unembedding-span assumption
Insufficient analysis of framework failure modes and scope limitations; no systematic evaluation of when TR/TL decomposition breaks down
Incomplete mechanistic explanation: geometric analysis is post-hoc; missing causal connection between attention patterns and hidden state transformations
Modest cross-dataset consistency of TR heads (Jaccard ~0.36) questions generalization despite 'task-invariant' framing
Missing ablations on key hyperparameters (3% threshold, 50-query initialization set size) and sensitivity analyses
TR ratio metric is somewhat artificial and doesn't guarantee true task recognition

strengths: Well-motivated framework bridging component-level and holistic perspectives on ICL with clear identified gap in prior work
Principled TSLA methodology addressing real limitations of DLA (label sensitivity, label competition) with theoretical support (Theorem 1)
Comprehensive experimental validation across 6 models and 8 tasks using multiple complementary approaches (correlation, ablation, perturbation, steering, geometric analysis)
Consistent empirical findings with clear interpretations: TR heads are task-invariant and overlap heavily with induction heads; TL heads are task-specific
Successfully reconciles multiple lines of prior work (induction heads as TR subset, task vectors capturing TR functionality) providing unifying framework
Extensive supplementary materials with cross-model replication and systematic analysis at multiple thresholds (3%, 5%, 10%, 20%)
Fine-grained geometric analysis revealing distinct mechanisms: TR heads align with task subspace, TL heads rotate within it
Addresses both classification and open-ended generation tasks, showing task-dependent effectiveness of different head types
weaknesses: TL score lacks formal theoretical justification unlike TR score (Theorem 1); connection between logit gap and task learning relies primarily on geometric intuition
Method assumes task semantics are captured in label unembedding subspace—while empirically validated, this assumption may not hold for abstract/ambiguous tasks
Novelty is somewhat incremental: TR/TL decomposition from Pan et al. (2023); main contribution is connecting to attention heads and geometric interpretation
Limited scope: all tasks are relatively simple (classification/constrained generation); no exploration of multi-step reasoning, code, or complex tasks
Threshold selection (3% of heads, 50 queries for identification) lacks systematic justification; while some sensitivity analysis provided in appendices, main paper would benefit
Causality claims occasionally overstated: phrases like 'TR heads drive alignment' rely on correlations (some moderate, e.g., ρ=0.53 in Fig 10b) and ablations showing necessity but not sufficiency
Limited comparison with alternative head identification methods; no computational cost analysis relative to baselines
Paper is dense with 88 supplementary figures; clearer highlighting of key insights in main text and better organization of appendices would improve accessibility

strengths: Theoretically motivated TSLA framework with formal probabilistic guarantees (Theorem 1) bridging component-level and holistic views of ICL
Exceptionally comprehensive experimental validation across 6 models and 7+ datasets with multiple experimental paradigms (ablations, perturbations, steering, geometric analysis)
Clear geometric mechanistic insights: TR heads align hidden states to task subspace while TL heads rotate within it—well-illustrated with visualizations and layerwise analysis
Successful reconciliation of prior findings (induction heads, task vectors) within TR/TL framework, explaining why TR-based task vectors restore ICL performance
Strong reproducibility support with extensive appendices covering ablation studies, design choice justification (e.g., 3% threshold sensitivity), statistical testing, and promised code release
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: TR/TL decomposition from Pan et al. (2023); main contribution is localizing existing framework to attention heads rather than introducing new mechanistic insights

Theoretical assumptions questionable: Theorem 1 assumes uniform distribution over Grassmannian which LLMs don't satisfy; assumption that demonstration labels' unembeddings span task subspace is strong and only empirically verified

Scope limitations significantly reduce generalizability: only simple classification and basic generation; 8-shot setting only; English-only; no exploration of 1-shot, large-shot, or complex reasoning tasks; only transformer-based architectures

Counterintuitive layer ordering (TR heads deeper than TL heads) insufficiently explained; Section G.7's 'logit-centric' distinction feels post-hoc and undermines the intuition that learning precedes recognition

Generation task results (SubjQA, review generation) partially contradict framework's generality: TL vectors outperform TR vectors in generation, suggesting task-type-dependent mechanisms; review generation uses only 200 synthetic examples with circular GPT labels

Causality claims overreach: ablations show necessity but not sufficiency; other components could compensate for removed heads; steering effectiveness doesn't definitively prove these heads carry core computation
Comparison to alternatives limited: DLA comparison relegated to appendix; missing discussion of simpler baselines; no comparison to other head identification methods

Multiple methodological choices under-justified or under-explored: sensitivity to task subspace definition, prompt templates, and different shot numbers; modest correlation values (ρ≈0.53-0.94) in geometric analysis suggest noise

strengths: Addresses an important research question about ICL mechanisms in LLMs with a framework that reconciles component-level and holistic perspectives
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple models (Llama, Qwen, Yi), datasets, and evaluation methods (ablations, perturbations, steering, geometric analysis)
Clear and intuitive geometric interpretation: TR heads align to task subspace while TL heads rotate within it, effectively visualized
Reconciles prior findings by showing induction heads function primarily as TR heads, helping clarify conflicting claims in literature
Complementary evaluation methods (ablations, input perturbations, steering, layerwise analysis) provide multiple angles of supporting evidence
Validates findings through correlation analysis, Jaccard coefficients, and rank correlations across datasets
weaknesses: Limited novelty in problem formulation: TR/TL decomposition derives from prior work (Pan et al. 2023); main contribution (TSLA grounding) is incremental application of existing circuit analysis frameworks

Weak theoretical justification: Theorem 1 assumes unrealistic Grassmannian-distributed task label embeddings and is somewhat tautological—it doesn't principly justify why projection norm is the right metric; assumption that labels lie in low-dimensional task subspaces lacks theoretical grounding
Causality claims insufficient: Ablations demonstrate necessity but not causation; steering experiments are limited and show only modest improvements; conflates correlation with causal mechanism

Critical task-dependence finding underexplored: Section 4.3 reveals TR/TL effectiveness reverses between classification and generation tasks, fundamentally undermining generality claims, yet receives cursory treatment rather than central investigation

Generalization concerns: Experiments limited to standard classification benchmarks (except one synthetic generation task); 8-shot setting with 200-example review dataset; no testing on truly novel or ambiguous-label tasks; narrow scope raises questions about applicability

Geometric mechanism claims are suggestive rather than definitive: Subspace Alignment uses cosine similarity as indirect proxy; layerwise correlations show association not causation; alternative explanations not ruled out

Arbitrary experimental choices with insufficient justification: Top 3% head selection justified post-hoc; many results sensitive to threshold choice; lack of principled basis for design decisions; 60-page appendix suggests extensive post-hoc tuning
Statistical rigor issues: Modest effect sizes (Jaccard overlap 0.36-0.47); p-values relegated to appendix; multiple hypothesis testing corrections not discussed; unclear whether effects exceed noise
Task subspace assumption empirically verified only for sentiment labels; not tested on tasks with non-hierarchical or ambiguous label semantics; no ablation on subspace dimensionality choices

Layer distribution finding (TR heads deeper than TL heads, Figure 3) lacks theoretical explanation; post-hoc justification via logit dynamics doesn't naturally follow from main framework; raises questions about completeness of theory

strengths: Clear motivation bridging component-level and holistic perspectives on ICL; addresses a meaningful gap in the literature
Novel TSLA framework with geometric interpretation and theoretical grounding (Theorem 1, though with limitations)
Exceptionally comprehensive experimental validation: 6 model architectures, 7 datasets, multiple validation approaches (overlap/correlation, ablations, perturbations, steering, geometric analysis)
Successfully reconciles conflicting findings about induction heads, showing they emerge as TR head subset for label-space recognition
Strong geometric insights: TR heads enable subspace alignment, TL heads perform within-subspace rotation; validated through multiple metrics
Excellent reproducibility: extensive appendices with detailed experiments, ablations, and supplementary analyses demonstrating serious commitment to reproducibility
Practical applications demonstrated: task vector design for improving zero-shot performance with clear mechanistic understanding
weaknesses: Novelty somewhat incremental: builds on Pan et al. (2023) TR/TL decomposition; main contribution is identifying which heads implement this decomposition rather than the decomposition itself

Theorem 1 has limited practical value: assumes unrealistic i.i.d. Grassmannian distributions, probability bounds become loose with many subspaces, primarily provides intuition rather than actionable guidance

TSLA design choices lack full justification: using demonstration labels to identify label-processing heads is circular reasoning; no exploration of alternative aggregations for TL score (Eq. 3); sensitivity to task subspace definition not thoroughly analyzed

Limited scope on task diversity: all primary experiments use 8-shot ICL only; predominantly classification tasks; generation experiments limited (movie reviews use GPT labels; SubjQA only book split); claim that TL heads matter more for generation based on limited evidence

Statistical rigor could be stronger: missing error bars/confidence intervals on most figures; no significance tests for most correlation/overlap comparisons; some claims based on visual inspection rather than statistical tests

Missing failure case analysis: when does TR/TL separation break down? No exploration of tasks with unclear label spaces or open-ended settings; no analysis of computational efficiency vs. simpler alternatives
Incomplete treatment of generation setting: unclear why TR heads fail in open-ended generation; forcing discrete sentiment labels may conflate findings; truly open-ended tasks not tested

Presentation could be clearer: paper is extensive and dense; core geometric intuition (Figure 1) deserves more textual explanation; choice of top 3% threshold for analyses not well justified in main text; some important results buried in appendices
